name: nasty
_comment: Every failure mode from research/12's table, on a timeline, over a short
lap so the whole thing runs in ~25 minutes. This is the script tickets
05 and 11 argue from: run it once and the answers to 'what does the app
do when X' stop being opinions.
Two things this file CANNOT do, because they are below the socket:
- a true black hole (peer vanished, writes unacknowledged, minutes of
silence before TCP notices) — use hotspot.sh blackhole
- an address change on DHCP lease renewal — use hotspot.sh
The 'silence' op below is the APP-level version: TCP is perfectly
healthy, the data just stopped. Both matter, and telling them apart is

faults._why: One sentence, two TCP writes. The most valuable single test here: a parser that assumes one read == one sentence passes everything else and fails on the water.
The mirror image — two sentences arriving in one packet.
Wrong checksum. Must be dropped, not parsed.
Cut off mid-sentence with no terminator. The next '$' must not be read as a continuation.
Binary junk mid-stream. Plotters emit this on power-up.
Ticket 05 q4: boat speed stops while wind keeps flowing. No off-the-shelf tool can do this. A sample built from a stale VHW and a fresh MWV is a lie.
Status V — the instrument saying 'I have no data'. Must not become 0 kn from dead ahead.
1 Hz drops to 0.2 Hz. Does 'complete enough set' logic stall?
App-level staleness: socket open and healthy, no bytes. Ticket 05 q4 and 11 q5.
Graceful FIN. The easy case — the app gets a close event and should reconnect.
Ticket 11 q4: plotter reboot. Every client dropped, port closed, back 30s later. From the phone this starts out identical to 'the phone left the boat'.
RST rather than FIN — the plotter losing power mid-sentence.
